# wranglarr configuration.  ${VAR} is expanded from the environment.

[server]
bind = "0.0.0.0"
port = 8787
# log_level = "info"

[storage]
root = "/backups"                 # backup sets live under <root>/<suite>/<timestamp>/
state_db = "/config/wranglarr.db" # settings + run history (SQLite)

[postgres]
host = "postgres"
port = 5432
user = "${POSTGRES_USER}"
password = "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
container = "arrs-postgres"       # for container updates

# Docker control is required for database and config-directory restores.
# Wranglarr confirms the app is stopped before writing, and restarts it after
# success only if it was running before. Failed restores leave it stopped for
# recovery; without Docker control these restores are refused.
# The socket also enables container updates ([updates] below).
[docker]
socket = "/var/run/docker.sock"

# Container image updates (needs [docker]).  Every app with `container` set is
# managed, plus Postgres and the VPN.  Checks only ask the registry (no pull);
# an update backs up the affected suite, pulls, recreates the container with
# the same settings and puts the old one back if the new one isn't healthy.
# UI changes are stored in the state db and win over this section.
[updates]
check_schedule = "0 */6 * * *"   # "" = only when you press Check now
auto_update = false              # true = apply available updates on auto_schedule
auto_schedule = "0 5 * * *"
backup_first = true
health_timeout = 300             # seconds for the new container to become healthy
# wranglarr itself is never part of auto_update.  self_update = true lets it
# replace its own container (through a helper) on self_schedule; the UI's
# Update now button does the same on demand.
self_update = false
self_schedule = "30 5 * * *"
# include_postgres = true        # [postgres] container
# include_vpn = true             # [vpn] container
# extra = ["prowlarr"]           # more containers to manage (no backup, health check only)
# exclude = ["arrs-postgres"]    # never touch these
# Per-container image tags. Omitted containers follow their deployed tag/digest.
# UI track choices override these; saving a track does not restart anything.
# [updates.tracks]
# wranglarr = "edge"             # development builds from main; "latest" = stable
# radarr = "develop"             # LinuxServer tag; Hotio calls this "testing"
# bazarr = "development"         # LinuxServer prereleases
# arrs-postgres = "17"           # stay on a major; major upgrades are refused

# Wire the apps together (System -> App connections): every download client
# into every arr (category = the arr's name), Sonarr/Radarr into Bazarr, every
# arr into Prowlarr.  `auto` does it at startup for links never made before;
# it never overwrites, and doesn't re-add what you removed by hand.
[connect]
auto = true

# Live status: wranglarr keeps a "wranglarr · live status" webhook in each arr
# and Prowlarr, so the pages show a change (a health warning cleared, an import)
# right away. `url` is where the apps reach wranglarr (default
# http://wranglarr:<port>); set it when they can't by that name.
[events]
enabled = true
# url = "http://192.168.1.10:8787"

# Shared-tunnel VPN status (compose.vpn.yaml): gluetun's control server.
# Only active when "vpn" is in WRANGLARR_ENABLED_APPS (compose.vpn.yaml adds it).
[vpn]
control_url = "http://vpn:8000"
api_key = "${GLUETUN_API_KEY}"
container = "arrs-vpn"            # for container updates

# A suite is a group of apps backed up together with one schedule + retention.
# The values here are defaults; anything changed in the UI is stored in the
# state db and wins over this file.
[[suite]]
name = "media"
schedule = "30 3 * * *"   # from the setup wizard
enabled = true
keep_last = 14
keep_days = 60

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "radarr"
  kind = "radarr"                         # radarr | sonarr | lidarr | readarr | prowlarr | whisparr
  url = "http://radarr:7878"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/radarr/config.xml"   # or: api_key = "${RADARR_API_KEY}"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/radarr"                  # copied into every version as radarr/config/
  databases = ["radarr", "radarr-log"]        # omit/empty for SQLite apps
  container = "radarr"                             # docker stop/start on restore + updates

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "sonarr"
  kind = "sonarr"
  url = "http://sonarr:8989"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/sonarr/config.xml"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/sonarr"                  # copied into every version as sonarr/config/
  databases = ["sonarr", "sonarr-log"]
  container = "sonarr"

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "lidarr"
  kind = "lidarr"
  url = "http://lidarr:8686"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/lidarr/config.xml"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/lidarr"                  # copied into every version as lidarr/config/
  databases = ["lidarr", "lidarr-log"]
  container = "lidarr"

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "prowlarr"
  kind = "prowlarr"
  url = "http://prowlarr:9696"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/prowlarr/config.xml"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/prowlarr"
  databases = ["prowlarr", "prowlarr-log"]
  container = "prowlarr"

  # Bazarr: zips are read from, and config restored into, its mounted /config.
  [[suite.app]]
  name = "bazarr"
  kind = "bazarr"
  url = "http://bazarr:6767"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/bazarr/config/config.yaml"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/bazarr"
  databases = ["bazarr"]
  container = "bazarr"

# Download clients: no backup API, so their /config is copied as-is into each
# version (logs excluded) and restored with the container stopped.
[[suite]]
name = "downloads"
schedule = "0 4 * * *"
keep_last = 14
keep_days = 60

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "qbittorrent"
  kind = "qbittorrent"
  url = "http://qbittorrent:8090"
  username = "${QBITTORRENT_USER}"
  password = "${QBITTORRENT_PASSWORD}"     # from .env: set it in the qBittorrent UI first
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/qbittorrent"
  container = "qbittorrent"

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "sabnzbd"
  kind = "sabnzbd"
  url = "http://sabnzbd:8080"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/sabnzbd/sabnzbd.ini"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/sabnzbd"
  container = "sabnzbd"

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "nzbget"
  kind = "nzbget"
  url = "http://nzbget:6789"
  username = "${NZBGET_USER}"                      # from .env: the image applies them at launch,
  password = "${NZBGET_PASS}"                      # nzbget.conf keeps the default
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/nzbget/nzbget.conf"   # fallback: ControlUsername/ControlPassword
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/nzbget"
  container = "nzbget"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared ("global") settings: define once, push to every app with the
# "Sync shared settings" button (or POST /api/suites/<suite>/sync).  Matched by
# name in each app: created if missing, updated otherwise.  `fields` are the
# app's own field names (what the app's UI posts); per-kind differences go in
# overrides.<kind>.  `apply_to` lists app kinds or app names; omit for all.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# [[shared.download_client]]
# name = "qBittorrent"
# implementation = "QBittorrent"      # configContract defaults to "<implementation>Settings"
# protocol = "torrent"
# priority = 1
# apply_to = ["radarr", "sonarr", "lidarr"]
# test = true                         # run the app's connection test before saving
#   [shared.download_client.fields]
#   host = "qbittorrent"
#   port = 8090                        # qBittorrent's port inside the network
#   username = "${QBITTORRENT_USER}"
#   password = "${QBITTORRENT_PASSWORD}"
#   useSsl = false
#   [shared.download_client.overrides.radarr.fields]
#   movieCategory = "radarr"
#   [shared.download_client.overrides.sonarr.fields]
#   tvCategory = "sonarr"
#   [shared.download_client.overrides.lidarr.fields]
#   musicCategory = "lidarr"

# [[shared.notification]]
# name = "Discord"
# implementation = "Discord"
# on_grab = true
# on_health_issue = true
# on_application_update = true
#   [shared.notification.fields]
#   webHookUrl = "${DISCORD_WEBHOOK}"

# ---- requests (profile seerr) ----------------------------------------------
# Seerr: requests and users in Postgres, settings.json (API key, Radarr/Sonarr
# entries, media server) in its /app/config.
[[suite]]
name = "requests"
schedule = "15 4 * * *"
keep_last = 14
keep_days = 60

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "seerr"
  kind = "seerr"
  url = "http://seerr:5055"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/seerr/settings.json"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/seerr"
  databases = ["seerr"]
  container = "seerr"
auth_steps: Apply it, in the stack directory: ./scripts/init.sh --auth  (it sets each app's login, and starts or removes wranglarr-gate for AuthTunnel).
Manual: wranglarr leaves the apps' logins alone; each app asks you to create one on first visit.
next_steps: Review ./.env (it holds secrets; mode 600).
In the stack directory run: ./scripts/init.sh  (POSIX shell / WSL; it generates and patches the arr configs, creates the databases and starts everything).

Open wranglarr at http://<this host>:8787 and create its admin account. It asks for a one-time setup code from its log: docker compose logs wranglarr. Then, under Account, turn on two-factor or add a passkey.
wranglarr will show a pending restore plan (2 item(s)); run it from the banner once the apps are up.

SQLite databases were found for: radarr, sonarr. Their config.xml is reused; after the first start, copy each database into Postgres (one command per app): see Importing-Existing-Apps in the docs (wiki/Importing-Existing-Apps.md).
Manual: wranglarr leaves the apps' logins alone; each app asks you to create one on first visit.
Trackers: add them on wranglarr's Indexers page (Torznab/Newznab feeds, Jackett, NZBHydra2, a Prowlarr) and pick which arrs get them.

[storage]
root = "/backups"                 # backup sets live under <root>/<suite>/<timestamp>/
state_db = "/config/wranglarr.db" # settings + run history (SQLite)

[postgres]
host = "postgres"
port = 5432
user = "${POSTGRES_USER}"
password = "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
container = "arrs-postgres"       # for container updates

# Docker control is required for database and config-directory restores.
# Wranglarr confirms the app is stopped before writing, and restarts it after
# success only if it was running before. Failed restores leave it stopped for
# recovery; without Docker control these restores are refused.
# The socket also enables container updates ([updates] below).
[docker]
socket = "/var/run/docker.sock"

# Container image updates (needs [docker]).  Every app with `container` set is
# managed, plus Postgres and the VPN.  Checks only ask the registry (no pull);
# an update backs up the affected suite, pulls, recreates the container with
# the same settings and puts the old one back if the new one isn't healthy.
# UI changes are stored in the state db and win over this section.
[updates]
check_schedule = "0 */6 * * *"   # "" = only when you press Check now
auto_update = false              # true = apply available updates on auto_schedule
auto_schedule = "0 5 * * *"
backup_first = true
health_timeout = 300             # seconds for the new container to become healthy

# replace its own container (through a helper) on self_schedule; the UI's
# Update now button does the same on demand.
self_update = false
self_schedule = "30 5 * * *"

# exclude = ["arrs-postgres"]    # never touch these

# UI track choices override these; saving a track does not restart anything.
# [updates.tracks]

# radarr = "develop"             # LinuxServer tag; Hotio calls this "testing"
# bazarr = "development"         # LinuxServer prereleases

# Wire the apps together (System -> App connections): every download client
# into every arr (category = the arr's name), Sonarr/Radarr into Bazarr, every
# arr into Prowlarr.  `auto` does it at startup for links never made before;
# it never overwrites, and doesn't re-add what you removed by hand.
[connect]
auto = true

# Live status: wranglarr keeps a "wranglarr · live status" webhook in each arr

[postgres]
host = "postgres"
port = 5432
user = "${POSTGRES_USER}"
password = "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
container = "arrs-postgres"       # for container updates

# Docker control is required for database and config-directory restores.
# Wranglarr confirms the app is stopped before writing, and restarts it after
# success only if it was running before. Failed restores leave it stopped for
# recovery; without Docker control these restores are refused.
# The socket also enables container updates ([updates] below).
[docker]
socket = "/var/run/docker.sock"

# Container image updates (needs [docker]).  Every app with `container` set is
# managed, plus Postgres and the VPN.  Checks only ask the registry (no pull);
# an update backs up the affected suite, pulls, recreates the container with
# the same settings and puts the old one back if the new one isn't healthy.
# UI changes are stored in the state db and win over this section.
[updates]
check_schedule = "0 */6 * * *"   # "" = only when you press Check now
auto_update = false              # true = apply available updates on auto_schedule
auto_schedule = "0 5 * * *"
backup_first = true
health_timeout = 300             # seconds for the new container to become healthy
# wranglarr itself is never part of auto_update.  self_update = true lets it
# replace its own container (through a helper) on self_schedule; the UI's
# Update now button does the same on demand.
self_update = false
self_schedule = "30 5 * * *"
# include_postgres = true        # [postgres] container
# include_vpn = true             # [vpn] container
# extra = ["prowlarr"]           # more containers to manage (no backup, health check only)
# exclude = ["arrs-postgres"]    # never touch these

# UI track choices override these; saving a track does not restart anything.
# [updates.tracks]

cases.toml:
# wranglarr configuration.  ${VAR} is expanded from the environment.

[server]
bind = "0.0.0.0"
port = 8787
# log_level = "info"

[storage]
root = "/backups"                 # backup sets live under <root>/<suite>/<timestamp>/
state_db = "/config/wranglarr.db" # settings + run history (SQLite)

[postgres]
host = "postgres"
port = 5432
user = "${POSTGRES_USER}"
password = "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
container = "arrs-postgres"       # for container updates

# Docker control is required for database and config-directory restores.
# Wranglarr confirms the app is stopped before writing, and restarts it after
# success only if it was running before. Failed restores leave it stopped for
# recovery; without Docker control these restores are refused.
# The socket also enables container updates ([updates] below).
[docker]
socket = "/var/run/docker.sock"

# Container image updates (needs [docker]).  Every app with `container` set is
# managed, plus Postgres and the VPN.  Checks only ask the registry (no pull);
# an update backs up the affected suite, pulls, recreates the container with
# the same settings and puts the old one back if the new one isn't healthy.
# UI changes are stored in the state db and win over this section.
[updates]
check_schedule = "0 */6 * * *"   # "" = only when you press Check now
auto_update = false              # true = apply available updates on auto_schedule
auto_schedule = "0 5 * * *"
backup_first = true
health_timeout = 300             # seconds for the new container to become healthy
# wranglarr itself is never part of auto_update.  self_update = true lets it
# replace its own container (through a helper) on self_schedule; the UI's
# Update now button does the same on demand.
self_update = false
self_schedule = "30 5 * * *"
# include_postgres = true        # [postgres] container
# include_vpn = true             # [vpn] container
# extra = ["prowlarr"]           # more containers to manage (no backup, health check only)
# exclude = ["arrs-postgres"]    # never touch these
# Per-container image tags. Omitted containers follow their deployed tag/digest.
# UI track choices override these; saving a track does not restart anything.
# [updates.tracks]
# wranglarr = "edge"             # development builds from main; "latest" = stable
# radarr = "develop"             # LinuxServer tag; Hotio calls this "testing"
# bazarr = "development"         # LinuxServer prereleases
# arrs-postgres = "17"           # stay on a major; major upgrades are refused

# Wire the apps together (System -> App connections): every download client
# into every arr (category = the arr's name), Sonarr/Radarr into Bazarr, every
# arr into Prowlarr.  `auto` does it at startup for links never made before;
# it never overwrites, and doesn't re-add what you removed by hand.
[connect]
auto = true

# Live status: wranglarr keeps a "wranglarr · live status" webhook in each arr
# and Prowlarr, so the pages show a change (a health warning cleared, an import)
# right away. `url` is where the apps reach wranglarr (default
# http://wranglarr:<port>); set it when they can't by that name.
[events]
enabled = true
# url = "http://192.168.1.10:8787"

# Shared-tunnel VPN status (compose.vpn.yaml): gluetun's control server.
# Only active when "vpn" is in WRANGLARR_ENABLED_APPS (compose.vpn.yaml adds it).
[vpn]
control_url = "http://vpn:8000"
api_key = "${GLUETUN_API_KEY}"
container = "arrs-vpn"            # for container updates

# A suite is a group of apps backed up together with one schedule + retention.
# The values here are defaults; anything changed in the UI is stored in the
# state db and wins over this file.
[[suite]]
name = "media"
schedule = "30 3 * * *"   # from the setup wizard
enabled = true
keep_last = 14
keep_days = 60

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "radarr"
  kind = "radarr"                         # radarr | sonarr | lidarr | readarr | prowlarr | whisparr
  url = "http://radarr:7878"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/radarr/config.xml"   # or: api_key = "${RADARR_API_KEY}"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/radarr"                  # copied into every version as radarr/config/
  databases = ["radarr", "radarr-log"]        # omit/empty for SQLite apps
  container = "radarr"                             # docker stop/start on restore + updates

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "sonarr"
  kind = "sonarr"
  url = "http://sonarr:8989"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/sonarr/config.xml"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/sonarr"                  # copied into every version as sonarr/config/
  databases = ["sonarr", "sonarr-log"]
  container = "sonarr"

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "lidarr"
  kind = "lidarr"
  url = "http://lidarr:8686"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/lidarr/config.xml"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/lidarr"                  # copied into every version as lidarr/config/
  databases = ["lidarr", "lidarr-log"]
  container = "lidarr"

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "prowlarr"
  kind = "prowlarr"
  url = "http://prowlarr:9696"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/prowlarr/config.xml"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/prowlarr"
  databases = ["prowlarr", "prowlarr-log"]
  container = "prowlarr"

  # Bazarr: zips are read from, and config restored into, its mounted /config.
  [[suite.app]]
  name = "bazarr"
  kind = "bazarr"
  url = "http://bazarr:6767"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/bazarr/config/config.yaml"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/bazarr"
  databases = ["bazarr"]
  container = "bazarr"

# Download clients: no backup API, so their /config is copied as-is into each
# version (logs excluded) and restored with the container stopped.
[[suite]]
name = "downloads"
schedule = "0 4 * * *"
keep_last = 14
keep_days = 60

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "qbittorrent"
  kind = "qbittorrent"
  url = "http://qbittorrent:8090"
  username = "${QBITTORRENT_USER}"
  password = "${QBITTORRENT_PASSWORD}"     # from .env: set it in the qBittorrent UI first
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/qbittorrent"
  container = "qbittorrent"

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "sabnzbd"
  kind = "sabnzbd"
  url = "http://sabnzbd:8080"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/sabnzbd/sabnzbd.ini"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/sabnzbd"
  container = "sabnzbd"

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "nzbget"
  kind = "nzbget"
  url = "http://nzbget:6789"
  username = "${NZBGET_USER}"                      # from .env: the image applies them at launch,
  password = "${NZBGET_PASS}"                      # nzbget.conf keeps the default
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/nzbget/nzbget.conf"   # fallback: ControlUsername/ControlPassword
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/nzbget"
  container = "nzbget"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared ("global") settings: define once, push to every app with the
# "Sync shared settings" button (or POST /api/suites/<suite>/sync).  Matched by
# name in each app: created if missing, updated otherwise.  `fields` are the
# app's own field names (what the app's UI posts); per-kind differences go in
# overrides.<kind>.  `apply_to` lists app kinds or app names; omit for all.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# [[shared.download_client]]
# name = "qBittorrent"
# implementation = "QBittorrent"      # configContract defaults to "<implementation>Settings"
# protocol = "torrent"
# priority = 1
# apply_to = ["radarr", "sonarr", "lidarr"]
# test = true                         # run the app's connection test before saving
#   [shared.download_client.fields]
#   host = "qbittorrent"
#   port = 8090                        # qBittorrent's port inside the network
#   username = "${QBITTORRENT_USER}"
#   password = "${QBITTORRENT_PASSWORD}"
#   useSsl = false
#   [shared.download_client.overrides.radarr.fields]
#   movieCategory = "radarr"
#   [shared.download_client.overrides.sonarr.fields]
#   tvCategory = "sonarr"
#   [shared.download_client.overrides.lidarr.fields]
#   musicCategory = "lidarr"

# [[shared.notification]]
# name = "Discord"
# implementation = "Discord"
# on_grab = true
# on_health_issue = true
# on_application_update = true
#   [shared.notification.fields]
#   webHookUrl = "${DISCORD_WEBHOOK}"

# ---- requests (profile seerr) ----------------------------------------------
# Seerr: requests and users in Postgres, settings.json (API key, Radarr/Sonarr
# entries, media server) in its /app/config.
[[suite]]
name = "requests"
schedule = "15 4 * * *"
keep_last = 14
keep_days = 60

  [[suite.app]]
  name = "seerr"
  kind = "seerr"
  url = "http://seerr:5055"
  api_key_file = "/arrconfig/seerr/settings.json"
  config_dir = "/arrconfig/seerr"
  databases = ["seerr"]
  container = "seerr"
